_comment: The stamped LINKED tier: how many matched translation units actually reach the
PC port's binary. This is a STAMP, not a live counter, and it cannot be anything
else from main: port/tools/linkage.py reads build/port/walk_window.map, which only
exists after an MSVC build of the port, and CI on main has no such build.
BEFORE STAMPING, LOOK FOR A BUILD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Every port lane carries its
own build tree, so a current walk_window.map is usually already on disk:
ls -la */build/port/walk_window.map
across the port worktrees, newest first, then run the tool against that root. The
first version of this file was stamped off a five-day-old branch while a map from
the night before sat unread one directory away, and published 26.5% when the real
figure was 34.5%. A stale stamp is still a real measurement, just of the wrong run.
To refresh: run `python port/tools/linkage.py [root]` and update the numbers below
together with branch, commit and measuredAt. Never move the count without also
moving the provenance fields - tools/tiers.py drops a stamp missing any of them,
which is the intended behaviour for a number nobody can trace.
basis records what the figure is a measurement OF. The port branches are not merged,
so this is the best single lane rather than a combined total. All seven live lanes,
lk5 3819. Overlapping but not identical seats, so the merged figure is higher and
the published number stays a floor.
This number moves ONE way: seating a new actor class, worth ~8-10 TUs each.
Enrolling free TUs does nothing, because the release build dead-strips whatever the
linked closure never references.
basis: integration branch port/link100 at its pushed tip b7a7580ea, measured against that tip's own battery build walk_window.map (C:/tmp/l1-int, gate INT11: tree clean, battery ALL GREEN at floor 10120 with every minigame scene row green, six proofs green including the opening-cutscene gate), and confirmed by the hosted-runner port-linkage workflow, which counts every push of port/** and the shipping branch on a GitHub Windows machine with no cartridge and has printed the local number for every push today. +17 over the late-afternoon stamp of 10114, +98 over the morning stamp of 10033, +1010 over the 2026-08-30 stamp of 9121. The shipping branch port-mount-noseat-cluster is fast-forwarded to the same commit. Since the 10114 stamp: the pointer-to-member rows that read an object field rather than a table (the dScMgBase family and the card scene's model sub-object), retired by seating the storage their writers copy from, with an address-targeted sweep of every relocation onto the known code words proving the seat complete and a comparison sentinel found that a naive seat would have broken silently; and the remaining single-row minigame tables plus the Curling pair and three ov060 tables, each behind a boot installer that checks every slot against the ROM before writing. Two hard facts came out of it: the actor half of the family is not a table problem (their matched sources define real C++ members that a flat-name face cannot reach, so one forwarder per class is the remaining work), and a table is takeable only if the constructor fills every cell in its span. Gated rungs since the last stamp: 10114 -> 10120 -> 10131. Remaining: about eight member-defining actor rows behind per-class forwarders, the Trampoline pair, six cutscene rows with two pointers-to-member per slot, then the wireless chain behind the ARM7 model (~175), the boot chain's refused arms, and guessed vtable bodies that need real decomp.
